chunks: The venerable Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babuwayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Talha ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdullah al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said:

Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him) passed by a people who were weeping. So he said: What are these people weeping over? So it was said: They are weeping over their sins. He said: Then let them abandon them, and they will be forgiven.

key_terms.توبة: Repentance; turning back to God by abandoning sin and seeking forgiveness
key_terms.مغفرة: Divine forgiveness; God pardoning the sins of the repentant

ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Isa (Jesus) say about weeping over sins and how to be forgiven?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates that Prophet Isa (Jesus, AS) once passed by a group of people weeping over their sins. He counselled them that the path to forgiveness lies not in mere weeping but in actually abandoning their sins. This hadith highlights a core Islamic teaching: sincere repentance requires both remorse and the decisive abandonment of sinful behavior. The message resonated deeply in early Muslim communities as a reminder that spiritual transformation demands action, not just emotional expression.

en.bilal-muhammad: Abu Ja`far Muhammad b. `Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babuwayh al-Qummi (ra) narrated to us. He said: My father (ra) narrated to us. He said: Sa`d b. `Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. `Isa narrated to us from his father from `Abdullah b. al-Mughira from Talha b. Zayd from Abi `Abdillah al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad (as). He said:

`Isa b. Maryam (as) passed by a people who were weeping. So, he said: What are these people weeping over? So, it was said: They are weeping over their sins. He said: Then, they should abandon them, and they will be forgiven.
